grammar_rules.summary: In most cases, the agent in a passive sentence is introduced by the preposition par.
grammar_rules.explanation: The preposition par is the default way to introduce the agent (the doer) in a passive construction.
usage: To indicate who performs the action in most passive sentences.
restrictions: Not universal: some passive sentences introduce the agent with de instead of par.
par remains the default choice for most passive sentences with an expressed agent.
conditions: The sentence is in the passive voice.
The agent (doer of the action) is expressed in the sentence.
exceptions: de replaces par after verbs of emotion or opinion
Some fixed passive expressions use de (e.g. aimé de tous)
agreement_rules: The past participle agrees with the subject, never with the agent
The agent introduced by par never triggers agreement
transformations: Il est respecté par ses collègues.
de -> par as the default agent preposition
